messages:
ella: KensaPay hitting a lot of 429s starting ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. Customer says spikes at the top of the minute, looks like per-key RPM limit. Example req id: req_7f3a9c2b. They attached a curl that fires 5 parallel requests from a cron job every minute.

samir: pulling edge logs now. I can already see repeated 'rate_limiter: drop' entries for that API key. Pattern: bursts at :00 - :01 each minute.

opsbot: BOT: X-RateLimit-Limit: 60, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 168 (seconds).

maria: @ella can you confirm whether they use our SDK or roll their own requests? SDKs have built-in leaky-bucket smoothing and jitter.

ella: customer uses a tiny in-house client. Cron spawns 5 worker processes, each does 12 requests in parallel -> effective 60 requests fired instantaneously at minute boundary, plus retries.

samir: that explains it. Their burst exceeds per-key RPM (60). Retries amplify it. Repro locally:
```
ab -n 300 -c 10 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
```
You can see our edge return 429 and the logs show the same throttling bucket id.

maria: quick customer-facing mitigations to recommend: 1) add exponential backoff with full jitter for 429s, 2) spread work across the minute (randomize cron start), 3) set client concurrency low (<=4), 4) use our SDK or token-bucket limiter with rpm cap.

ops_lead: long-term: we should offer smoothing at gateway for short bursts (configurable per-customer) and an opt-in "burst buffer" for partners. For this case, support can offer a temporary quota bump. @infra_bot can we do a 4x temporary RPM increase for this key for 24h?

infra_bot: Created INF-3421. Temporary quota change is possible but needs approval. Proposed: bump to 240 RPM, 24h window, then auto-revert.

samir: alternative quick-fix: enable per-key "leaky-bucket smoothing" on edge for that key now (rate-limit window: 60rpm smoothed to 1rps). That will significantly reduce 429 spikes without a quota change. I can flip that if infra approves.

ella: customer asked for "how to prove it's client-side" — Samir, can you attach a log snippet showing the burst timestamps?

samir: here are two lines from edge logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T09:12:00Z edge[req_7f3a9c2b] rate_limiter=drop key=kensa-prod bucket=60 remaining=0
2026-03-17T09:12:00Z edge[req_7f3a9c2c] rate_limiter=drop key=kensa-prod bucket=60 remaining=0
2026-03-17T09:12:01Z edge[req_7f3a9c2d] rate_limiter=ok   key=kensa-prod bucket=60 remaining=58
```
Shows cluster of drops at the same second.

maria: I'll send them a short checklist: randomize cron, reduce parallelism, implement client-side limiter, honor Retry-After, consider SDK. Offer to enable smoothing or temporary bump while they deploy fixes.

ops_lead: approved temporary smoothing ON for key for 12h while customer rolls changes; infra will monitor. No billing change.

ella: I'll reply with the checklist + timeline and ask for a follow-up trace after they apply jitter. Thanks all :thumbsup:

opsbot: BOT: Ticket SUP-5589 created for customer communication thread.
